release_notes: LeadForge 2.0 & CRM Anti-Shaving Vault. The landing compiler becomes a two-stage pipeline: Analyze (up to 15 ZIP/HTML/PHP bundles, static inspection — source-network detection across 13 CPA signatures, forms and field inventory, foreign counters, encoding and GEO checks) feeds Build with three integration modes — Auto (detect + route), Cross-Network (cut the old network's order/send/api handlers and re-seat the landing on the target network) and Raw (strip foreign counters and hostile scripts, inject the ClickID bridge without a backend). After each build, Live Auto QA posts a QA-Test-Lead through the real order.php bridge and scores it 0-100% (form structure, bridge response, dual logging, thank-you redirect) while keeping analytics pristine. The CRM grows a full lead vault (crm_leads): raw vs E.164 phone, UTM/adset/ad attribution, and the exact network request/response dump — fed in-process by generated order.php, via the public /crm-ingest endpoint for bundles hosted elsewhere, or manually from the panel. Postbacks reconcile S2S statuses and run the shave detector: a lead rejected after a provably valid E.164 delivery and a 200 from the network becomes a Suspected Shave with an evidence pack for the network's support; 24h-silent leads flag as lost in transit and same-phone repeats mark as duplicates. Fixes: the order.php bridge was dying on the 3s PHP-landing budget mid-network-call (bridge files now get max(timeout, 25s)), router.php swallowed /postback.php, /order.php and /crm-ingest with empty 200s on the dev server, and both suite pages now follow the global theme system (no hardcoded gradients, text-inverse on primary for the neon theme).
